newsitem.title: USA: Fore gets French library network contract.
newsitem.headline: Fore gets French library network contract.

text.p: Fore Systems Inc said Wednesday it had been selected by the French National Library to build Europe's largest end-to-end network using high-speed asynchronous transfer mode computer network technology.

In a statement from Paris, Fore said the installation will include 300 of its ATM switches and connect more than 3,500 workstation users on a network capable of transmitting multimedia data at speeds of up 155 megabits per second.
It said the end-to-end network will link multiple branches of the French National Library, one of the world's oldest public libraries.
A Fore spokeswoman said the deal represents the largest number of users with direct ATM connections that Fore has ever announced.
ATM technology is a high speed method for delivering multimedia text, voice and video, which many analysts consider to represent the future of office computer network technology.
The ATM network will be put into operation during the first half of 1997, the company said.

Fore, a Pittsburgh, Pa.-based leader in ATM technology, said it will install its ForeRunner ASX-1000 and ASX-200BX ATM switches in a network backbone linked to ForeRunner ASX-200WG switches running in workgroups composed of personal computers.
The high-performance ATM network will enable new applications including multimedia retrieval of library archives and digitized documents.
Library officials chose the ATM network for its capacity to provide rapid information access and speed document retrieval time considerably, the company said.
The network also will be able to provide services like teleconferencing and Internet access.

The network will be designed by Fore and implemented by Phillips Communication D'Enterprise, a Fore network integrator and distributor in France. Cie des Machines Bull will provide systems integration for the project.
Fore Systems stock was up 2-5/16 at 40-5/8 at midday Tuesday.
